item.title: Kochi Vegetables, Yuzu and Myoga Ginger — Guide
item.description: Kochi’s warm, sunny climate and abundant rainfall make it one of Japan’s leading producers of vegetables and aromatic crops. The prefecture grows the nation’s largest share of ginger, myoga (a fragrant ginger bud used as a garnish and pickle), eggplant, and green peppers, while its mountain villages — Umaji among them — are famous for yuzu, the fragrant citrus that flavours so much Japanese cooking. These aromatic ingredients are the backbone of Tosa cuisine, brightening its seared bonito, hot pots and pickles.
